 Advertisement New England governors ask federal government for $3B more in heating assistance
 Advertisement Updated: 6:24 PM EST Nov 10, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Adam Sexton Political Director New England governors ask federal government for $3B more in heating assistance
 Updated: 6:24 PM EST Nov 10, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Adam Sexton Political Director MANCHESTER, N.H. — With cooler weather approaching, all six New England governors are asking the federal government for more money to pay for home heating aid.
 The Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program, or LIHEAP, helps qualified families with their winter heating bills.
 Advertisement "I think this is really important that the federal government also recognize that we're going to have greater needs this season," Gov. Kelly Ayotte said.
 The governors are calling on Congress to add $3 billion to the program, saying higher-than-normal energy costs are straining the program.
 >> Download the free WMUR app to get updates on the go << 
 "I am deeply concerned about how my seniors, how my families are going to stay warm," said Executive Councilor Janet Stevens. "I have retired principals going back to teaching at a substitute level because they're concerned about filling up their tanks."
 State energy officials told the Executive Council on Tuesday that their internal price tracking shows home heating oil starting to trend downward, although not by much.
 "It is starting to look like the prices are starting to come down a little bit," said Joshua Elliott, deputy commissioner of the Department of Energy. "We do a survey of all the oil, propane and other fuel dealers across the state. Bit of a spoiler alert, we're going to publish numbers tomorrow, it looks like we're seeing about a 20-cent per gallon decrease."
 "Twenty cents, that is something," said Executive Councilor Karen Liot Hill. "But we're talking about, last year was just over $3 a gallon. We're almost at $7 a gallon. So 20 cents, that's helpful, but that's not addressing the fact that it's almost twice as expensive to fill a tank of oil. That's another $500. So maybe if it's only going to be $450 more than it was last year to fill a tank, that's still a huge burden."
 While there's no waiting list for help right now, Ayotte said it's important that Washington address the regional request for more funding in a serious and timely manner.
 "I think there is a sense of urgency," Ayotte said. "This is the important time to act on this issue, and I hope the Congress acts on it. This has always been a bipartisan issue."
 The $3 billion being requested would bring total program funding to $7 billion this year.
 Anyone who needs help with their heating bills can apply for LIHEAP by contacting their county Community Action Agency. Find a list of numbers here .
 The state also has additional resources residents may be able to take advantage of.
